opportunities.title: Fewer approval clicks. Same ability to catch mistakes?
opportunities.summary: Test whether showing the consequences of an AI-proposed change makes human review easier without hiding errors.
opportunities.contribution: An experiment design and reusable review tasks—not another agent framework.
opportunities.feasibility: Start with fictional ticket-routing changes. A later study needs participants and supervisor agreement.
opportunities.venture: An approval interface for small automation teams. Buyer demand is untested.
opportunities.next: Create six example cases and a feasible evaluation plan before recruiting anyone.
opportunities.evidence: Adjacent research exists; this specific comparison still needs a prior-work check.
opportunities.question: Can consequence summaries reduce review effort while preserving consequential-error detection?
opportunities.measure: Errors caught · review time · perceived effort
opportunities.risk: Faster approval could mean less scrutiny.
opportunities.alternative: Ordinary diffs, approval dialogs and checklists
opportunities.reason: Closest match to your interest in approval fatigue.

opportunities.title: The AI was right. Did the workflow still fail?
opportunities.summary: Separate a wrong AI answer from a correct answer delivered twice, sent to the wrong place, or never completed.
opportunities.contribution: A fault-labelled trace benchmark comparing output checks with execution checks.
opportunities.feasibility: Use small synthetic traces on a laptop. Real-system validation would be a later step.
opportunities.venture: A testing component for automation builders. Existing evaluation tools are strong alternatives.
opportunities.next: Define a trace format, twelve examples and a baseline comparison.
opportunities.evidence: n8n already offers evaluations; operational complaints motivate investigation but do not prove a research gap.
opportunities.question: Do execution invariants detect failures that output-only evaluations miss?
opportunities.risk: Could reduce to ordinary systems testing rather than an AI thesis.
opportunities.alternative: n8n evaluations, logs and unit tests
opportunities.reason: Strong engineering fit; does not need participant recruitment.

opportunities.title: When your smart home should say “I’m not sure”
opportunities.summary: Study how occupancy estimates should behave when room sensors and the total number of people disagree.
opportunities.contribution: A robustness study of probabilistic estimates and an explicit unknown state.
opportunities.feasibility: Begin with a three-room simulation. No sensors or real household monitoring required.
opportunities.venture: More understandable home automation. Consumer demand and energy savings are not established.
opportunities.next: Specify three baselines and ten sensor-conflict examples.
opportunities.evidence: Home Assistant already supports Bayesian sensor fusion. The possible gap is robustness to contradictory signals.
opportunities.question: When do whole-home constraints help, and when is an unknown answer safer?
opportunities.risk: A favourable simulator may not reflect real homes.
opportunities.alternative: Bayesian sensors, timers and manual overrides
opportunities.reason: An outside-software-industry option with an Applied AI core.

opportunities.title: Replay a workflow failure—and see what went wrong
opportunities.summary: Drop a small execution trace into a browser and see duplicate actions, missing completion events and broken steps.
opportunities.contribution: A visual timeline and an exportable incident report using six sample failures.
opportunities.feasibility: One local web page, one JSON format, no accounts or integrations.
opportunities.venture: Potential debugging aid for solo automation builders. Willingness to pay is unknown.
opportunities.next: Build the sample-trace viewer, verify each failure and publish a small demo.
opportunities.evidence: Workflow evaluations already exist. The test is whether this makes a failure easier to understand.
opportunities.question: Can you understand a workflow incident faster than by reading raw logs?
opportunities.risk: May offer little beyond a good log viewer.
opportunities.alternative: n8n logs, JSON viewers and custom scripts
opportunities.reason: Recommended for a small, testable first engineering release.

opportunities.title: Why did changing my food preferences do nothing?
opportunities.summary: Show how food preferences affect a comparison—and explain ties, missing information and unchanged rankings.
opportunities.contribution: A comparison demo with twelve fictional products and transparent score contributions.
opportunities.feasibility: Use fictional products and simple non-medical preferences. No food API or nutritional advice.
opportunities.venture: An explanation feature for shopping apps. One complaint is not proof of a market.
opportunities.next: Create six preference-change scenarios and a clear side-by-side comparison.
opportunities.evidence: One reported issue plus existing Open Food Facts matching APIs; the cause of that issue is unconfirmed.
opportunities.question: Is explaining an unchanged result more useful than a simple product filter?
opportunities.measure: Six hand-checked scenarios · clear unknown states
opportunities.risk: A plain attribute table might explain it better.
opportunities.alternative: Product filters and Open Food Facts matching
opportunities.reason: A small consumer-facing alternative with no AI dependency.

opportunities.title: An annual bill is not always “divide by twelve”
opportunities.summary: Explain the difference between a bill’s monthly average and what you need to put aside before its due date.
opportunities.contribution: A household timeline with six fictional bills, reserves and transparent calculations.
opportunities.feasibility: A local page with deterministic arithmetic; no bank connection or real financial records.
opportunities.venture: A household planning utility or existing-app feature. Spreadsheet substitution is strong.
opportunities.next: Build the timeline and verify six date, reserve and rounding cases.
opportunities.evidence: A forum question title is a lead only; the underlying discussion has not yet been verified.
opportunities.question: Does a timeline explain irregular bills better than a spreadsheet?
opportunities.measure: Correct dates · exact rounding · understandable amounts
opportunities.risk: The problem may already be solved well by spreadsheets.
opportunities.alternative: Spreadsheets, savings pots and budgeting apps
opportunities.reason: Quick to test with a familiar consumer problem.
